claims.text: As-printed high-entropy-alloy components produced by rapid laser additive manufacturing inherently contain microporosity.
As-printed high-entropy-alloy components contain residual stresses.
As-printed high-entropy-alloy components exhibit minor dimensional inaccuracies.
A single in-situ laser re-melting pass improves the dimensional precision of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
A single in-situ laser re-melting pass improves the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
A single in-situ laser re-melting pass reduces fabrication-induced defects in additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Laser re-melting causes localized microstructural homogenization.
The local thermal treatment generated by re-melting promotes stress relaxation.
Partial re-solidification during re-melting reduces porosity.
Partial re-solidification during re-melting improves inter-layer bonding.
Stress relaxation, reduced porosity, and improved inter-layer bonding produce enhanced dimensional stability.
Re-melted components will have higher tensile strength than otherwise identical as-printed components.
Re-melted components will have greater toughness than otherwise identical as-printed components.
The predicted benefits require sufficient re-melting penetration and uniform thermal treatment.
High laser reflectivity or extremely thin geometry may prevent the predicted benefits.
Non-optimized laser parameters can cause over-melting or introduce new defects.
There are currently no direct empirical studies specifically evaluating this re-melting intervention in high-entropy alloys.
